Design/review only; no process launch, no server behavior change.

existing_dispatch_design_chain.note: A layered, all-disabled-by-default 'future launch' design already exists in code, unwired to any @mcp.tool(). This review documents the chain so Codex/owner can decide the next gated step deliberately.

layers.artifact: phase2_orchestration_contract (static safety allowlist origin, referenced in later modules' docstrings)
layers.role: Defines the static human-configured LAUNCHABLE_BINARIES / adapter allowlist that every later layer mirrors.

Validates a would-be dispatch command against the static allowlist (LAUNCHABLE_BINARIES=(claude,codex); deepseek_manual stays manual-only) and writes an append-only audit entry ONLY. LAUNCH_IMPLEMENTED=False constant; no subprocess/exec/fork/shell import anywhere.

Wraps B105 as a strictly READ-ONLY view: plan_command_readonly (validated plan, no audit write even though the underlying dryrun planner could emit one -- calls plan_dryrun(audit=False)), audit_summary_readonly, readonly_tool_report (combines both). Adds a read-only collision preflight (would_collide) against the same task-card JSONL the tasking collision guard scans.

Pure schema (LaunchRequest/LaunchDecision/ProcessLogEntry dataclasses, ProcessState enum) plus append-only JSONL audit persistence for a FUTURE gated launch queue. attempt_start() always raises LaunchDisabledError. Requires BOTH GEOAI_TASK_MCP_ALLOW_LAUNCH=1 AND GEOAI_TASK_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES=1 (both default '0') before evaluate_launch() could ever return anything but blocked_launch_disabled -- and no launcher exists yet even if both were set.
layers.gap: Neither module is imported by server.py. Codex has NO MCP-visible view of the disabled launch-queue state today; it is only reachable via direct Python import in tests.

layers.layer: future / not yet a task card

layers.role: Would be the FIRST module in this chain permitted to actually spawn a process, and only behind both env gates.

safe_dispatch_contract_recommendation.runner_topic_identity_guard: Every dispatch-adjacent tool already takes explicit runner/topic/task_id parameters (geoai_task_auto_pickup, geoai_task_pending_for_runner, geoai_cli_adapter_plan_readonly). A future launch tool MUST (a) accept explicit task_id+runner+topic, (b) echo them back verbatim in its result alongside the task's own WORKER_CONTRACT_JSON.task_id/runner/topic, and (c) the dispatched worker must self-verify the match before reading beyond read_first or writing anything -- this is the same task_identity_guard already mandated for every worker contract, just enforced one layer earlier at dispatch time instead of only at worker-start time.
safe_dispatch_contract_recommendation.allowed_writes_guard: git staging/commit (taskctl.py stage / guard-staged) must stay CLI-only and is NOT exposed as an MCP tool today, and should not become one: broadening a worker's write surface must remain the dispatched worker's own responsibility under its task card's allowed_writes, never something Codex-via-MCP can expand from outside.
safe_dispatch_contract_recommendation.review_queue_handoff: Already sufficient today with zero process-launch capability: geoai_task_review_queue / geoai_task_review_summarize / geoai_task_codex_handoff / geoai_task_codex_handoff_markdown give Codex a full read-only view of tasks awaiting review (grouped by topic/runner, validation commands, allowed_writes, derived risk), and geoai_task_mark_review / geoai_task_mark_done (write-gated) let Codex finalize without any worker process ever being launched via MCP.
safe_dispatch_contract_recommendation.no_process_launch_by_default: Verified: LAUNCH_IMPLEMENTED / launch_enabled() are hardcoded False (not env-toggle-dependent) in cli_adapter_dryrun.py, launch_queue_contract.py, and cli_adapter_readonly_tool.py; attempt_start() always raises LaunchDisabledError; server.py contains no subprocess/os.system/os.popen/os.exec/os.fork/os.spawn/Popen(/shell=True/pty.spawn pattern (same forbidden-pattern check already enforced by test_mcp_stdio_subprocess_client_smoke_b109_v1.sh and reused here).

sufficient_today_for: Non-mutating preview of which task an auto-pickup WOULD claim (auto_pickup_dryrun)
Actual task claim/start (auto_pickup, write-gated, requires GEOAI_TASK_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES=1)
Codex review-queue triage and handoff (review_queue, review_summarize, codex_handoff, codex_handoff_markdown)
Supervisor-loop state derivation for a task_id (supervisor_loop_status)
Read-only PREVIEW of a validated future dispatch command with no execution (cli_adapter_plan_readonly / audit_summary_readonly / report_readonly)
missing_before_any_process_launch_can_be: MCP-visible read-only wiring for the disabled launch_queue_contract/launch_queue_persist state (currently invisible to Codex over MCP; only reachable via direct Python import in tests) -- low-risk, additive, mirrors the existing B106 pattern.

An actual launcher implementation: none exists anywhere in the codebase today (LAUNCH_IMPLEMENTED=False in every layer). Before one can exist it must: require BOTH GEOAI_TASK_MCP_ALLOW_LAUNCH=1 AND GEOAI_TASK_MCP_ALLOW_WRITES=1; reuse the SAME static LAUNCHABLE_BINARIES=(claude,codex) allowlist (deepseek_manual stays manual-only permanently); write to the SAME append-only launch_queue_persist audit log; enforce the runner/topic/task_id identity-guard echo above; never itself perform git stage/guard-staged/commit (that stays the dispatched worker's own CLI-only step); and land as its own explicitly reviewed gated-enablement task with a refusal-by-default regression test plus an isolated-sandbox positive-path test.

A learned adapter/runner/topic selection policy: today's task->runner assignment is the static taskctl auto-pickup claim logic. Per this project's neural-control-first doctrine, the eventual choice of which adapter/runner/topic to dispatch must become a LEARNED routing+abstain policy (already named in code comments as MCP_NEURAL_LAUNCH_ROUTING_MIGRATION_V1, not yet a task card in the manifest) rather than the current static allowlist/FIFO, which is an acceptable bootstrap only while that migration ticket stays open and tracked.

summary: B251 orchestration review: 20 live MCP tools (16 read-only, 4 write-gated) already give Codex full discover/preview/review/finalize capability with zero process-launch surface. A layered disabled-by-default dispatch design (B104 static allowlist -> B105 dryrun validator -> B106 read-only MCP view, live -> B119 launch-queue schema+audit, NOT yet MCP-wired) already anticipates a future gated launcher, but no launcher exists anywhere in the codebase (LAUNCH_IMPLEMENTED=False everywhere) and none should until a dedicated gated-enablement task adds dual env-gate requirement, identity-guard echo, and reuse of the existing append-only audit trail. Adapter/runner/topic selection remains a tracked-but-unbuilt neural migration, not a runtime cue router.
